editorial.editors_note: As we mourn Peter Neumann, the pioneer who spent half a century chronicling our systemic failures, we are reminded that true engineering is carved out of hard physics and structural rigor, not the ephemeral scaffolding of unaccountable governance models; yet, the choice to return to foundational mechanics remains entirely within our hands.
editorial.emphasis: The tension between deterministic physical systems and fragile automated governance.

To ensure graceful closures and enable connection reuse, systems must explicitly drain incoming buffers or use lingering closes before shutting down.
